correctness.rationale: The pair of weighted fusion frames with a single index I={1}, V_1=W_1=R^2 and v_1=w_1=1 is woven: the only whole-block weaves select the same full space and have bounds exactly 1. Its local frames F_1=(e1,e2) and G_1=(e2,e1) are each orthonormal bases with bounds 1, satisfying the printed uniform hypotheses of Bhandari Theorem 3.1. But atomic selection of the first atom from F and the second atom from G is (e1,e1), which has zero frame energy on e2 and thus is not a frame. The claimed implication from fusion weaving to ordinary atomwise flattened weaving therefore fails. The reverse implication holds: for every outer sigma choose atomic tau={(i,j):i in sigma}; if all atomic weaves have uniform L,U and local bounds a<=A_i,C_i, B_i,D_i<=b, then a E_sigma(x)<=Q_sigma(x)<=b E_sigma(x) and L||x||^2<=Q_sigma(x)<=U||x||^2 imply L/b<=E_sigma/||x||^2<=U/a. We checked the 2024 theorem's actual quantifiers and its forward proof (only sigma subsets of outer I), and the blockwise condition in 2018 Lemma 2.2. Corrected statement distinguishes atomic from blockwise quantification; no attempt to claim novelty for blockwise characterization.

value.rationale: A concrete correction of an incorrect equivalence in published frame theory is mathematically useful despite the small witness: it distinguishes independent local-vector failure from whole-subspace stability, prevents incorrect transfer of universal weaving bounds, and records the precise one-way statement and the known blockwise substitute. The two-dimensional one-block example is minimal and fully meets the source's assumptions; it is not an unmotivated artificial slice.

limitations: Does not refute blockwise local-frame equivalence or classify sufficient atomwise assumptions.
Interpretation risk if author intended nonstandard blockwise use of ordinary term "weaving frames".
